BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON = "Interface\\Icons\\INV_Misc_QuestionMark"
-- **The reference's action-bar constant block (ActionButton.lua:1-9).** Every one of these -- was cited in comments across this file and MultiBars.xml and DEFINED nowhere, so an addon -- reading them got nil. `zBar.lua:40` is the shape: -- -- to = to or value.max or NUM_ACTIONBAR_BUTTONS -- for i = from, to do -- 'for' limit must be a number -- -- Found by the use-probe, which is the only column that touches anything. -- -- `CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE` used to be withheld from this list on the grounds that it is the -- reference's MUTABLE page cursor and we did not page the main bar — "defining it as a -- frozen 1 would hand every addon a number that is silently wrong forever". That reasoning -- was right and is now discharged rather than overruled: the bar pages, the global is live -- state the paged-id formula reads, and it is declared with the paging verbs below rather -- than here among the true constants. A frozen 1 would still be a lie; this one moves. NUM_ACTIONBAR_PAGES = 6 NUM_ACTIONBAR_BUTTONS = 12 BOTTOMLEFT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE = 6 BOTTOMRIGHT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE = 5 LEFT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE = 4 RIGHT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE = 3
-- Ref ActionButton.lua:4 / UIParent.lua: the flash blink period and the range-check cadence. ATTACK_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME = 0.4 TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME = 0.2
-- "Lock ActionBars" (ref UIOptionsFrame.lua:102-103 — uvar LOCK_ACTIONBAR, default "0"). -- The reference declares it in its options window; ours lives with the bar it locks, which -- is this codebase's rule for every stock global (1128/1134): the assignment sits beside its -- consumers, and the options row CAPTURES it rather than restating a default of its own. -- Read by the drag guards below and by the pet bar's (PetActionBar.xml, the ref's own second -- consumer at PetActionBarFrame.lua:270/278); driven by the Action Bars page and by the -- TOGGLEACTIONBARLOCK binding the option's tooltip promises (decision 1136). LOCK_ACTIONBAR = "0" RegisterForSave("LOCK_ACTIONBAR")
-- CooldownFrame_SetTimer moved to Cooldown.xml (the ref's own file split) — the bag -- slots share it, so it loads before both consumers.
-- One button's HotKey corner — the ref's ActionButton_UpdateHotkeys law in FULL since -- 1008 (closing 0997's raw-token residue): the ABBREVIATED binding text through the -- GetBindingText the ref specifies (ours, in UIParent.xml — one modifier abbreviates, "s-2"; -- two or more collapse to the ref's "·"), and with NO binding the ref's no-binding -- leg — an empty label the OnUpdate range timer fills with the RANGE_INDICATOR dot -- while out of range (until 1008 that leg was multibar-only; now any unbound slot, -- main bar included, wears it). A harness with no registered bindings paints nothing. function BenillaActionButton_PaintHotkey(button) local key = GetBindingKey(button.bindingCommand) local text if GetBindingText then text = GetBindingText(key, "KEY_", 1) else -- lone-file harness (the shipped manifest always has UIParent.xml first): -- the raw token, the MicroMenu.xml fallback idiom. text = key or "" end button.noBindingLabel = (text == "") button.hotkey:SetText(text) end
-- Every button's label, repainted on UPDATE_BINDINGS (a rebind, a set switch, the seed). function BenillaActionBar_UpdateHotkeys() for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS) do BenillaActionButton_PaintHotkey(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS[i]) end end
-- Every live action button — the main bar's 12 plus the multibars' (MultiBars.xml joins -- at OnLoad). The fan-out roster for the bar-level events below: the ref registers the -- feedback events per-button; our bar-level fan needs the full set in one place. BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS = {}
-- ── Main-bar paging (ref ActionButton.lua l.1-12 and l.63-101) ─────────────────────── -- The main bar has six pages, and we already hold every slot they address: the app owns -- the authoritative 1..120 action table, so the DATA for pages 2-6 was always there and -- only the page SELECTOR was missing. Its absence was on screen, not just in the API — -- the page arrows below shipped as art with no OnClick, which this file's own comment -- admitted ("ART ONLY - we have no bar paging, so the clicks are no-ops"). -- -- `Bartender2.lua:686` is the corpus tell: three bare `ChangeActionBarPage()` calls, and -- the addon died on the nil global at session start. CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE = 1 -- "Table of actionbar pages and whether they're viewable or not" (the reference's own -- comment). The page walk below honours it rather than counting, which is what makes the -- whole thing work: a page an extra bar already displays must not ALSO be reachable on the -- main bar, or paging up shows you the twelve actions already on screen beside it. -- -- **This is the shipped START state, not a constant: it FOLLOWS the four bar toggles.** -- All six pages are viewable here because all four extra bars now ship hidden (decision -- 1500 — they are player options, off by default), and `MultiActionBar_Update` -- (MultiBars.xml) does the arithmetic from then on: a bar that comes up takes its page out -- of the cycle, a bar that goes down puts it back. Blanking two rows at declaration was -- only ever right because visibility was static (0270's always-on bottom pair), and the -- moment the player can move it a declaration cannot be the answer. VIEWABLE_ACTION_BAR_PAGES = {1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1}
-- `ChangeActionBarPage()` takes NO arguments — every reference caller sets -- CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE first and then calls this to apply it (l.79, l.100), and -- Bartender2 calls it bare. -- -- Upstream it is a client binding; here it is FrameXML, deliberately. Our paged action id -- is computed in Lua by `BenillaActionBar_ActionFor`, so the page IS this global and the -- only work left for the verb is the repaint the reference gets by firing -- ACTIONBAR_PAGE_CHANGED. Addons CALL this, they never replace it, so the divergence is -- unobservable from Lua — unlike a name we shadow, which is 1222's class. function ChangeActionBarPage() for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS) do BenillaActionButton_Update(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS[i]) end end
function ActionBar_PageUp() local page = CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE + 1 local nextPage for i = page, NUM_ACTIONBAR_PAGES do if VIEWABLE_ACTION_BAR_PAGES[i] then nextPage = i break end end -- Past the last viewable page, wrap to 1 — the reference wraps to the LITERAL 1 here -- rather than to the first viewable page, which is its own asymmetry with PageDown -- (which rescans). Kept, because it is observable: with page 1 blanked, paging up off -- the end lands on a page the down-walk would have skipped. CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE = nextPage or 1 ChangeActionBarPage() end
function ActionBar_PageDown() local page = CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE - 1 local prevPage for i = page, 1, -1 do if VIEWABLE_ACTION_BAR_PAGES[i] then prevPage = i break end end if not prevPage then for i = NUM_ACTIONBAR_PAGES, 1, -1 do if VIEWABLE_ACTION_BAR_PAGES[i] then prevPage = i break end end end CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE = prevPage ChangeActionBarPage() end
-- Seat a TOP-LEVEL frame that anchors INTO the bar art (the bag bar + backpack toggle, -- BagFrame.xml; the micro-button row, MicroMenu.xml) one frame level above the art, so its -- icons draw over the bar plate instead of under it. -- -- Why it's needed: those frames are top-level, so they default to a LOWER frame level than -- the bar's own art (a child hierarchy — the ExpBar's dwarf notches + the metal/well art sit -- at the bar's child level). Frame level dominates the flat painter's order, so the bar art -- would paint OVER them — the ring shows but the centered icon is fully covered (the "empty -- rings, no bag icons" bug). The bar's OWN 12 buttons avoid this by being CHILDREN of the art -- frame (child-over-parent). (SetParent onto the art frame would be the structural twin, but -- the engine keys draw order at creation and does not re-key on a runtime reparent, so the -- explicit level is the reliable lever.) Lives here, with the frame it's about, because two -- files now need it — it began as BagFrame.xml's private BenillaBagBar_SeatAboveActionBar. function BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(frame) local art = getglobal("MainMenuBarArtFrame") if art then frame:SetFrameLevel(art:GetFrameLevel() + 1) end end
-- ── The keyring's half of the bar (ref MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing, MainMenuBar.lua -- l.174-183; decision 0765) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The keyring is not just a button bolted onto the bar: the bar's two RIGHT-hand strips are -- re-textured to a variant plate that has a socket for it, and the performance meter slides -- 8px further left out of the way. Both atlases are 256-wide 43px strips at the same on- -- screen size and anchors, so only the file + TexCoords change (UI-MainMenuBar-KeyRing is -- 256x128 and holds exactly the two bands the ref names: 0.3359375 * 128 = 43px each). -- -- Called by KeyRingButton's own OnEvent (BagFrame.xml). Everything is nil-guarded: -- this file loads without BagFrame.xml in several harnesses, and BagFrame.xml loads without -- this one in ~25 bag/bank/escape/merchant tests — either way the missing half no-ops. -- -- DIVERGENCE (decision 0765): the ref latches this ON forever the first time HasKey() is -- true, via the saved variable SHOW_KEYRING (and pulses the button for 60s to announce it). -- This engine has no saved variables, and a session-scoped latch would leak across a -- character switch — showing a keyring on a character with no key — so the state is derived -- from HasKey() on every BAG_UPDATE instead, in BOTH directions. Observably identical -- unless you destroy your last key, which then un-shows the keyring rather than leaving an -- empty one behind. The 60s pulse is out, consistently with decision 0304's "no button -- pulse" for the micro buttons. function MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing() local show = HasKey and HasKey() -- The two right-hand strips (MainMenuBarTexture2 at x=+128, Texture3 at x=+384), -- keyring plate or the ordinary dwarf plate. The dwarf coords are this file's own -- authored ones (see the strips below) — restated here because this is the only code -- that ever changes them back. local strips = { { name = "MainMenuBarTexture2", keyring = 0.6640625, keyringBottom = 1.0, dwarf = 0.33203125, dwarfBottom = 0.5 }, { name = "MainMenuBarTexture3", keyring = 0.1640625, keyringBottom = 0.5, dwarf = 0.08203125, dwarfBottom = 0.25 }, } for _, strip in ipairs(strips) do local tex = getglobal(strip.name) if tex then if show then tex:SetTexture("Interface\\MainMenuBar\\UI-MainMenuBar-KeyRing") tex:SetTexCoord(0, 1, strip.keyring, strip.keyringBottom) else tex:SetTexture("Interface\\MainMenuBar\\UI-MainMenuBar-Dwarf") tex:SetTexCoord(0, 1, strip.dwarf, strip.dwarfBottom) end end end -- The performance meter's recess moves with the plate: -227 without the keyring, -- -235 with it (ref l.180). Its own comment at the foot of this file has the geometry. local perf = getglobal("MainMenuBarPerformanceBarFrame") local bar = getglobal("MainMenuBar") if perf and bar then perf:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", bar, "BOTTOMRIGHT", (show and -235) or -227, -10) end local button = getglobal("KeyRingButton") if button then if show then button:Show() else button:Hide() end end -- Losing the last key with the keyring open would strand an orphan window; the ref -- can't reach this state (its latch is one-way), so this is ours to decide. local frame = getglobal("BenillaKeyRingFrame") if frame and not show and frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() end end
-- The wire/API action id the MAIN bar's button i displays (the vanilla page formula). -- INTERNAL to BenillaActionButton_Action below — the ONLY caller. A button path that -- reaches past it computes a MAIN-bar id for a multibar button (base ignored), which -- reads as "the slot below": the tooltip hover did exactly that until 2026-07-21. function BenillaActionBar_ActionFor(index) local offset = GetBonusBarOffset() local base = 0 if offset > 0 then base = (6 + offset - 1) * 12 else -- The paged main bar. A bonus page (stance/form/stealth) OUTRANKS it, which is -- why this is the else arm and not an addition: the reference's own -- `ActionButton_GetPagedID` takes the bonus branch first. base = (CURRENT_ACTIONBAR_PAGE - 1) * 12 end return base + index end
-- The action id a specific BUTTON displays: the ref forks on the parent frame's NAME -- (ActionButton_GetPagedID:446-467 — MultiBarBottomLeft ⇒ page 6, MultiBarBottomRight ⇒ -- page 5, else the paged/bonus formula); we carry the fork as data — a fixed per-button -- page base set at OnLoad (MultiBars.xml), nil for the bonus-paged main bar. -- **Adopt a button that never ran our OnLoad.** -- -- Our handlers read a region cache (`button.icon`, `.count`, `.cooldown`, …) that -- `BenillaActionButton_OnLoad` fills. An addon inheriting `ActionBarButtonTemplate` gets -- those handlers and supplies its OWN `<OnLoad>`, which REPLACES the template's rather -- than chaining — so ours never runs and every one of those reads was nil. zBar.xml:7 is -- the corpus shape; it died in OUR file at `ActionBar.xml:529` on `button.icon`. -- -- Resolving from the derived names is not a fallback bolted on: it is exactly what our -- OnLoad does, and what the REFERENCE does on every access (`ActionButton_Update` reads -- `getglobal(this:GetName().."Icon")` each time rather than caching). We cache because it -- is cheaper; this is the same lookup for the buttons that never got cached. -- -- It deliberately does NOT join `BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS`. That roster is the event fan-out -- for OUR bars, and a foreign button's owner drives its own updates — adding it would have -- us repainting somebody else's button behind their back. function BenillaActionButton_Adopt(button) if not button or button.icon then return end local n = button:GetName() if not n then return end button.icon = getglobal(n .. "Icon") button.hotkey = getglobal(n .. "HotKey") button.count = getglobal(n .. "Count") button.flash = getglobal(n .. "Flash") button.border = getglobal(n .. "Border") button.cooldown = getglobal(n .. "Cooldown") button.flashing = button.flashing or 0 button.flashtime = button.flashtime or 0 -- The grid count, same posture: a foreign button reaching ActionButton_HideGrid with -- no count would raise on the arithmetic, which is 1199's class of silent-wrong-shape. button.showgrid = button.showgrid or 0 end
function BenillaActionButton_Action(button) -- `index` falls back to the button's ID, which is where the REFERENCE reads it from: -- `ActionButton_GetPagedID` uses `this:GetID()`, and our `.index` is only that value -- cached at OnLoad. A button that inherits `ActionBarButtonTemplate` and wires its own -- OnLoad — zBar.xml:7 does exactly this — never runs ours, so `.index` is nil while -- `GetID()` is set from the XML `id=`. Before the fallback, our own handler raised -- `ActionBar.xml:228: arithmetic on local 'index'` on somebody else's button. -- -- Still nothing? Action 0, which is not a real slot: every reader answers nil for it -- and the button draws empty. Deliberately not an early `return nil` — the callers are -- arithmetic all the way down, and a nil would move the raise rather than remove it. local index = button.index or button:GetID() or 0 if button.base then return button.base + index end return BenillaActionBar_ActionFor(index) end
-- Hover: SetAction's pure delegation (decision 0276 — a SPELL slot renders the spell -- tooltip with its rank column, an ITEM slot the shared item renderer; ref -- ActionButton_SetTooltip). The re-enter keeps it live across page flips. -- Anchor: ref ActionButton_SetTooltip (ActionButton.lua l.366-372) branches on the -- UberTooltips CVar — "1" → the default corner, else beside the button, LEFT for the bars -- that sit at the screen edge and RIGHT for the rest. This branch was collapsed to the "1" -- leg until B230, on the reason that benilla shipped no CVar state for anything to move -- it; 0954 ended that and cvars.rs now registers the key (default "1", byte-read — the -- evidence lives on that row), so the fork is live and the stock look is unchanged. -- -- The ref's LEFT set is {MultiBarBottomRight, MultiBarRight, MultiBarLeft} — the three bars -- that sit at (or against) the right edge, so their plates have to open toward the centre. -- All three exist here now: the two VERTICAL bars landed with 1219 and became player -- options with 1500, and this comment said "only the first exists" for as long as that was -- true. Membership is by FRAME, not by visibility — a hidden bar is never hovered anyway. function BenillaActionButton_OnEnter(button) BenillaActionButton_Adopt(button) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets if GetCVar("UberTooltips") == "0" then -- `parent and` first: an orphan button's nil parent would otherwise match a nil -- MultiBarRight in a harness that loaded no multibars, and anchor the wrong way. local parent = button:GetParent() local edgeBar = parent and (parent == MultiBarBottomRight or parent == MultiBarRight or parent == MultiBarLeft) if edgeBar then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end else GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, button) end GameTooltip:SetAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) end
function BenillaActionButton_OnLoad(button, index, base, commandPrefix) button.index = index button.base = base button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.hotkey = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "HotKey") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") button.flash = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Flash") button.border = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Border") button.cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") -- Ref ActionButton_OnLoad:104-106: the flash/range state the OnUpdate loop drives. button.flashing = 0 button.flashtime = 0 button.rangeTimer = nil -- ref ActionButton_OnLoad l.104: the empty-well grid count starts at zero. button.showgrid = 0 -- Every bar button carries its binding COMMAND (0997 main bar, 1008 multibars): -- the caller names the command family (MultiBars.xml passes MULTIACTIONBAR1/2BUTTON -- — the ref's own bar↔page mapping quoted there); nothing passed = the main bar's -- ACTIONBUTTON. The label paints from it here and repaints on UPDATE_BINDINGS. button.bindingCommand = (commandPrefix or "ACTIONBUTTON") .. index BenillaActionButton_PaintHotkey(button) table.insert(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS, button) -- BOTH mouse buttons, ref-verbatim (ActionButton_OnLoad, ActionButton.lua:108-109): -- an action button is a two-button button. The OnClick body reads no `arg1` — in the -- ref either button runs the same PickupAction/UseAction fork — so right-click USES -- the action, which is how food and spells are used off the bar. Without this the -- widget default ({"LeftButtonUp"}, `benilla_ui::script::button`) silently swallowed -- every right-click on the bar (director's report B200). button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 0216 §3/§7): click-carry and drag share one downstream path -- by construction (OnClick/OnDragStart both call PickupAction; OnReceiveDrag calls -- PlaceAction — ref ActionBarFrame.xml:12-38). Both buttons drag, ref-verbatim too -- (l.108) — a started drag suppresses the click, so right-press-and-move relocates the -- action while right-click-in-place still uses it. Both drag ends honour LOCK_ACTIONBAR -- since 1136 — see the guards themselves for what the lock does and does not stop. button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton", "RightButton") BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
-- Ref ActionBarFrame.xml:12-22's fork verbatim: shift picks up, else uses (checkCursor=1 — -- the engine routes a click-with-payload to PlaceAction instead, decision 0216 §7). function BenillaActionButton_OnClick(button) BenillaActionButton_Adopt(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if IsShiftKeyDown() then PickupAction(action) else UseAction(action, 1) end BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
-- The lock (ref ActionBarFrame.xml:23-38, both handlers wrapped in `if LOCK_ACTIONBAR ~= "1" -- then … end`). Note what the reference does NOT guard, and neither do we: the shift-click -- pick-up in OnClick above (its l.12-22 fork runs PickupAction unconditionally). So the lock -- stops the *drag*, and shift-click stays the deliberate way to move an action with the bar -- locked — which is what makes the setting usable rather than a wall. function BenillaActionButton_OnDragStart(button) BenillaActionButton_Adopt(button) if LOCK_ACTIONBAR == "1" then return end PickupAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
function BenillaActionButton_OnReceiveDrag(button) BenillaActionButton_Adopt(button) if LOCK_ACTIONBAR == "1" then return end PlaceAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
-- The default ACTIONBUTTON1..12 key bindings (ref Bindings.xml:121-127: keys 1..9,0,-,= -- run ActionButtonDown on keystate "down" and ActionButtonUp on "up" via runOnUp), both -- re-expressed from ActionButton.lua:15-28/30-45 and routed here from the app's key feed. -- DOWN pushes the button only from NORMAL; UP fires the action only from PUSHED — the -- state pair is both the pushed visual and the debounce (a key-repeat DOWN or a stray UP -- is a no-op). Calls UseAction DIRECTLY with NO checkCursor argument — unlike the -- mouse-click fork above, a keybind never places (decision 0216 §7: the ref itself never -- routes ActionButtonUp through OnClick, so this no longer goes through Click() either — -- the two entry points share the id formula, not the click path). The ref's -- BonusActionBar fork is not modeled (no bonus bar frame). -- -- SIGNATURES ARE THE 1.12 ONES (decision 1199): `ActionButtonDown(id)` / -- `ActionButtonUp(id, onSelf)`, the shapes an addon calls. These two never took a frame — -- they take the bar INDEX in both clients — so nothing here changes but the names and the -- restored `onSelf`, which rides through to UseAction's third argument exactly as the ref's -- l.56 does (our binding accepts and ignores it — `script/action.rs`). function ActionButtonDown(id) local button = getglobal("ActionButton" .. id) if ( button:GetButtonState() == "NORMAL" ) then button:SetButtonState("PUSHED") end end
function ActionButtonUp(id, onSelf) local button = getglobal("ActionButton" .. id) if ( button:GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" ) then button:SetButtonState("NORMAL") UseAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button), 0, onSelf) -- Ref ActionButtonUp:55-59: the checked ring reflects the use immediately. BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) end end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateState:261-267 — the checked ring: the current action (Attack -- while auto-attacking, the in-flight cast) or the live auto-repeat spell. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if ( IsCurrentAction(action) or IsAutoRepeatAction(action) ) then button:SetChecked(1) else button:SetChecked(0) end end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateUsable:269-283, verbatim colors: usable white; out of power the -- blue-grey 0.5/0.5/1.0 on icon AND ring; otherwise-unusable the 0.4 grey icon only. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateUsable(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) local normalTexture = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "NormalTexture") local isUsable, notEnoughMana = IsUsableAction(action) if ( isUsable ) then button.icon:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) normalTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) elseif ( notEnoughMana ) then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.5, 0.5, 1.0) normalTexture:SetVertexColor(0.5, 0.5, 1.0) else button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) normalTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateCooldown:294-298. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateCooldown(button) local start, duration, enable = GetActionCooldown(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(button.cooldown, start, duration, enable) end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateFlash/StartFlash/StopFlash/IsFlashing:469-496: the red blink on -- an engaged Attack button / a live auto-repeat, toggled by the OnUpdate loop below. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateFlash(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if ( (IsAttackAction(action) and IsCurrentAction(action)) or IsAutoRepeatAction(action) ) then BenillaActionButton_StartFlash(button) else BenillaActionButton_StopFlash(button) end end
function BenillaActionButton_StartFlash(button) button.flashing = 1 button.flashtime = 0 BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) end
function BenillaActionButton_StopFlash(button) button.flashing = 0 button.flash:Hide() BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) end
-- Ref ActionButton_OnUpdate:384-428, minus the tooltip refresh (no per-button tooltip -- yet): the 0.4 s flash toggle, and the 0.2 s range recheck — a bound slot's label -- tints red/grey, an unbound one wears the RANGE_INDICATOR dot (both legs the ref's, -- unified in 1008 — the SCOPE note). function ActionButton_OnUpdate(elapsed) BenillaActionButton_Adopt(this) local button = this if ( button.flashing == 1 ) then button.flashtime = button.flashtime - elapsed if ( button.flashtime <= 0 ) then local overtime = -button.flashtime if ( overtime >= ATTACK_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME ) then overtime = 0 end button.flashtime = ATTACK_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME - overtime if ( button.flash:IsVisible() ) then button.flash:Hide() else button.flash:Show() end end end if ( button.rangeTimer ) then button.rangeTimer = button.rangeTimer - elapsed if ( button.rangeTimer <= 0 ) then if ( IsActionInRange(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) == 0 ) then -- An UNBOUND button has no label to tint: paint the ref's -- RANGE_INDICATOR dot instead (net ref behavior — red dot iff out of -- range). Since 1008 the fork is the binding text itself (any bar's -- slot can be bound or bare now), not which bar owns the button. if button.noBindingLabel then button.hotkey:SetText("●") end button.hotkey:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.1, 0.1) else if button.noBindingLabel then button.hotkey:SetText("") end button.hotkey:SetVertexColor(0.6, 0.6, 0.6) end button.rangeTimer = TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME end end end
-- the ref's count law (ActionButton.lua:285-292), re-expressed here. The gate is -- IsConsumableAction, NOT "count > 0": a consumable you have run out of shows a literal -- "0", and an item that is not consumable (a mount, a trinket, a bag) shows nothing at -- all, however many copies you hold. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateCount(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if IsConsumableAction(action) then button.count:SetText(GetActionCount(action)) else button.count:SetText("") end end
-- ── The reference's names, so an addon that hooks them is reached ────────────────────── -- -- The 1.12 customisation model is "replace a global and the client calls your replacement" -- (Bagnon does it to `ToggleBackpack`; `zBar`/`zBarEx` do -- `SetScript("OnShow", ActionButton_Update)`; `CT_BarMod` calls `ActionButton_Update()` -- outright). Wherever our UI calls a `Benilla`-named function and never the reference's -- name, every one of those addons is SILENTLY INERT — the override is installed and never -- invoked. A survey cannot see it; it loads addons and fires events but never clicks. -- -- These are ADAPTERS, not renames, and the distinction is the whole point: the reference's -- contract is `this`-shaped and no-argument, ours takes the button explicitly. Renaming -- would let `TipBuddy`'s `originalUnitFrame_OnEnter()` reach us with a nil frame — reachable -- but broken, which is worse than inert. The adapter publishes the reference's SHAPE and -- delegates. -- -- NOT adapted, and named so nobody assumes it was missed: `ActionButton_OnLoad`. Ours is -- `(button, index, base, commandPrefix)` and the reference's takes nothing — the extra -- arguments are real state our per-container registration needs, so no adapter can supply -- them. That is the per-button event registration change already at the top of the arc -- queue, not a naming fix. -- **`ActionButton_OnLoad()` — the reference's own, taking nothing and reading `this`.** -- -- This sat at the top of the arc queue for the whole wave, recorded as unadaptable: ours -- takes `(button, index, base, commandPrefix)` and the reference's takes none, so "no -- adapter can supply them". Reading ref ActionButton.lua:103-119 shows that was wrong — -- the reference derives all three from `this` and it is our own signature that caches -- them: -- -- index -> `this:GetID()` (what ActionButton_GetPagedID reads) -- commandPrefix -> `this.buttonType`, a field the BAR sets, "ACTIONBUTTON" by default -- (ref l.118 `ActionButton_UpdateHotkeys(this.buttonType)`) -- base -> not an OnLoad concept at all; the reference forks on the PARENT's -- NAME at read time. A foreign bar ("zBar1") matches no multibar, so -- the paged/bonus formula applies — which is what leaving `base` nil -- already does here. -- -- The events are registered on the BUTTON, as the reference does, and reach it through the -- `<OnEvent>` this change adds to `ActionBarButtonTemplate`. " " .. progress .. " / " .. width) local color = FACTION_BAR_COLORS[reaction] ReputationWatchStatusBar:SetStatusBarColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) ReputationWatchBar:Show() ReputationWatchStatusBar:SetFrameLevel(MainMenuBarArtFrame:GetFrameLevel() - 1)

-- ── The watch bar's own handlers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Chunk functions rather than the reference's inline bodies, so the departures below have -- somewhere to be explained (ReputationFrame.xml's chunk-boundary rule). -- `ref-ReputationFrame.xml` l.996-1035 is the specification. -- -- PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD is benilla's ADDITION (decision 1094's own): our faction feed only -- fires once the catalog and the player's race/class are up, which can be a tick or two -- after world entry, and the max-level rail must be right from the first frame. -- Coming up with the cvar set means the numerals were meant to be pinned on all along. function BenillaWatchBar_OnShow() if GetCVar("statusBarText") == "1" then ShowWatchedReputationBarText("lock") end UIParent_ManageFramePositions() end
-- ── The exhaustion tick (ref-MainMenuBar.lua ExhaustionTick_*) ──────────────────────── -- The round marker riding the XP bar at the point where rested XP runs out, plus the -- pale fill between the bar's value and that point. NOTHING of the specification is cut -- here any more: the two ReputationWatchBar guards that used to be missing (the -- max-level-plus-rep tick hide, ref-MainMenuBar.lua l.51-54, and the -- rep-bar-replaced-the-xp-bar hide, l.69-71) were dropped as UNREACHABLE — the watch bar -- could never show — and it shows now, so both are live in ExhaustionTick_Update below. -- The MainMenuBarMaxLevelBar guard is live since 1094. -- -- The rest-state palette, keyed by GetRestState's own state id (ref-MainMenuBar.lua -- l.56-66 is the specification; the two rgb triples are its). Rested is the light blue, -- normal the purple; the ids above 2 are the beta-era tiers the live server never sends and -- the reference paints nothing for either. BENILLA_REST_STATE_COLOR = { [1] = { r = 0.0, g = 0.39, b = 0.88 }, [2] = { r = 0.58, g = 0.0, b = 0.55 }, }
function ExhaustionTick_OnLoad() local tick = this tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_XP_UPDATE") tick:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_EXHAUSTION") tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LEVEL_UP") tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_UPDATE_RESTING") end
function ExhaustionTick_Update() local tick = this if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" or event == "PLAYER_XP_UPDATE" or event == "UPDATE_EXHAUSTION" or event == "PLAYER_LEVEL_UP" then local playerCurrXP = UnitXP("player") local playerMaxXP = UnitXPMax("player") local exhaustionThreshold = GetXPExhaustion() local exhaustionStateID = GetRestState() -- The ref's beta-eras leftover: the tired/exhausted tiers (id >= 3) park the tick -- at the bar's RIGHT end. The live server never produces them (GetRestState's -- binding note) — kept because the ref keeps it. if exhaustionStateID >= 3 then tick:SetPoint("CENTER", "MainMenuExpBar", "RIGHT", 0, 0) end if not exhaustionThreshold then tick:Hide() ExhaustionLevelFillBar:Hide() else local exhaustionTickSet = max(((playerCurrXP + exhaustionThreshold) / playerMaxXP) * MainMenuExpBar:GetWidth(), 0) tick:ClearAllPoints() if exhaustionTickSet > MainMenuExpBar:GetWidth() or MainMenuBarMaxLevelBar:IsShown() then tick:Hide() ExhaustionLevelFillBar:Hide() else tick:Show() tick:SetPoint("CENTER", "MainMenuExpBar", "LEFT", exhaustionTickSet, 0) ExhaustionLevelFillBar:Show() ExhaustionLevelFillBar:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "MainMenuExpBar", "TOPLEFT", exhaustionTickSet, 0) end end -- ref-MainMenuBar.lua l.51-54: at max level with a watched faction the strip the -- tick rides is the REPUTATION bar, which has no rested pool — hide the tick. if UnitLevel("player") == MAX_PLAYER_LEVEL and ReputationWatchBar:IsShown() then ExhaustionTick:Hide() end end -- The rest-state paint (only these two events repaint it, the ref's own split): one -- rest state, one hue, worn by all three pieces at once — the strip's fill, the pale -- wash up to the tick at a sixth alpha, and the tick's own ADD highlight. A state with -- no row paints nothing, which is what the reference's if/elseif does for every id but -- these two (and GetRestState answers nil off a wire that has not spoken yet, which -- indexes to the same nothing). if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" or event == "UPDATE_EXHAUSTION" then local rest = BENILLA_REST_STATE_COLOR[GetRestState()] if rest then MainMenuExpBar:SetStatusBarColor(rest.r, rest.g, rest.b, 1.0) ExhaustionLevelFillBar:SetVertexColor(rest.r, rest.g, rest.b, 0.15) ExhaustionTickHighlight:SetVertexColor(rest.r, rest.g, rest.b) end end -- ref-MainMenuBar.lua l.69-71, the function's own last statement: the watch bar has -- REPLACED the XP bar (max level), so there is no XP strip left for the tick to sit on -- whatever the event was. Distinct from the guard above, which only runs on the four -- position events; this one runs on every one. if ReputationWatchBar:IsShown() and not MainMenuExpBar:IsShown() then ExhaustionTick:Hide() end end
-- The tick's tooltip (ref-MainMenuBar.lua ExhaustionToolTipText, the live branches only — -- its own dead commented-out code is not carried). Two callers, two postures: hovering -- the TICK anchors the plate beside it (flipped to whichever side has room); the armed -- 1 s timer from the BAR hover instead APPENDS the line to the already-open newbie tip, -- gated on canAddRestStateLine. EXHAUST_TOOLTIP4 (time to fully rested) needs -- GetTimeToWellRested, which is nil on this wire — the line simply never renders, -- faithfully (the binding's note). function ExhaustionToolTipText() if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS ~= "1" then local x, y = ExhaustionTick:GetCenter() if ExhaustionTick:IsVisible() then if x >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(ExhaustionTick, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(ExhaustionTick, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end else GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, UIParent) end end local exhaustionStateID, exhaustionStateName, exhaustionStateMultiplier = GetRestState() local exhaustionThreshold = GetXPExhaustion() exhaustionStateMultiplier = exhaustionStateMultiplier * 100 local exhaustionCountdown = nil if GetTimeToWellRested() then exhaustionCountdown = GetTimeToWellRested() / 60 end local tooltipText = format(EXHAUST_TOOLTIP1, exhaustionStateName, exhaustionStateMultiplier) local append = nil if IsResting() then if exhaustionThreshold and exhaustionCountdown then append = format(EXHAUST_TOOLTIP4, exhaustionCountdown) end elseif exhaustionStateID == 4 or exhaustionStateID == 5 then append = EXHAUST_TOOLTIP2 end if append then tooltipText = tooltipText .. append end if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS ~= "1" then GameTooltip:SetText(tooltipText) else if GameTooltip.canAddRestStateLine then GameTooltip:AddLine("\n" .. tooltipText) GameTooltip:Show() GameTooltip.canAddRestStateLine = nil end end end
-- Driven from the XP BAR's OnUpdate (the ref wires it there, not on the tick — the timer -- only ever counts while the mouse is on the bar, which is what arms it). function ExhaustionTick_OnUpdate(elapsed) if ExhaustionTick.timer then if ExhaustionTick.timer < 0 then ExhaustionToolTipText() ExhaustionTick.timer = nil else ExhaustionTick.timer = ExhaustionTick.timer - elapsed end end end
-- ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.104-110 (the overlay child's OnLoad): the numerals wiring lives -- in the OVERLAY frame's own OnLoad because there its FontString is guaranteed -- materialized; the bar's lockShow starts at the not-hovered refcount. function BenillaExpBarOverlay_OnLoad() if SetTextStatusBarText then -- engine tests load file subsets MainMenuExpBar.lockShow = 0 SetTextStatusBarText(MainMenuExpBar, MainMenuBarExpText) end end
-- ── The performance ("ping") meter ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.344-407: a 16x64 frame in the bar's own right-hand recess whose -- 20x66 bar texture is TINTED green/yellow/red by the connection's latency, plus an -- all-points button on top for the hover tooltip. The thresholds, the 10 s poll and the -- inline handlers below are the ref's, re-expressed out of its XML into named functions. -- The meter shows LATENCY ONLY: 1.12 never scales the bar's height, only its color. PERFORMANCEBAR_LOW_LATENCY = 300 PERFORMANCEBAR_MEDIUM_LATENCY = 600 PERFORMANCEBAR_UPDATE_INTERVAL = 10
-- ref-GlobalStrings.lua l.2659 / l.2689 / l.2746 (enUS), fallback form — see the XP bar's -- note above for why these never override a real localized install. MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL = MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL or "Latency:" MILLISECONDS_ABBR = MILLISECONDS_ABBR or "ms" NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY or "The average time it takes to talk with the game server. A low latency will display as a green bar, higher latencies will be yellow or even red. Consistently high latencies may indicate a problem with your Internet connection."
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnLoad(frame) frame.hover = nil -- 0, not the interval: the ref's first OnUpdate tick runs the poll immediately, so the -- bar is never briefly untinted (its texture is grey until the first SetVertexColor). frame.updateInterval = 0 end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_TooltipText() local _, _, latency = GetNetStats() return MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL .. " " .. latency .. MILLISECONDS_ABBR end
-- ref l.389 (the held-open refresh) and l.400 (OnEnter), both the same call: -- BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL.." "..latency..MILLISECONDS_ABBR, -- 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY) -- So the reference hover is TWO lines — the number, then the wrapped explanation — seated -- at the default screen corner, not beside the meter (GameTooltip.xml, decision 0661). function BenillaPerformanceBar_ShowTooltip(owner) if not GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(owner, BenillaPerformanceBar_TooltipText(), 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY) end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) if frame.updateInterval > 0 then frame.updateInterval = frame.updateInterval - elapsed return end frame.updateInterval = PERFORMANCEBAR_UPDATE_INTERVAL local _, _, latency = GetNetStats() if latency > PERFORMANCEBAR_MEDIUM_LATENCY then MainMenuBarPerformanceBar:SetVertexColor(1, 0, 0) elseif latency > PERFORMANCEBAR_LOW_LATENCY then MainMenuBarPerformanceBar:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 0) else MainMenuBarPerformanceBar:SetVertexColor(0, 1, 0) end -- Held-open tooltips re-read the number on the same 10 s beat (the ref's own refresh). if frame.hover then BenillaPerformanceBar_ShowTooltip(frame) end end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnEnter(button) MainMenuBarPerformanceBarFrame.hover = 1 BenillaPerformanceBar_ShowTooltip(button) end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnLeave() MainMenuBarPerformanceBarFrame.hover = nil if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end end
